title: Oregon revenue forecast shows about $245M more for 2027-29
summary: The November forecast raised expected 2027-29 general fund revenue by roughly $245M, driven by gains among higher-income Oregonians; state economists cautioned that such booms tend to correct. The forecast is the last one before Kotek's Dec 1 budget.

title: Kotek unveils policy proposals for a second term
summary: Kotek's reelection platform has four pillars, one of them improving K-12 schools. School items include reaching the national average for instructional time by the end of a second term, cutting chronic absenteeism, tougher diploma requirements, literacy, universal preschool and revisiting enrollment-based funding. The plan did not say how the school goals would be paid for.
key_facts: Instructional time to national average by end of second term

title: Gov. Tina Kotek's plan for ambitious academic goals gets scrutiny, then hesitant support from Board of Education
summary: The State Board of Education approved SB 141 achievement targets due in 2029-30 (e.g. 8th-grade math proficiency from 29% to 52%), with escalating interventions for districts that miss them. ODE's director said the targets need no new money; some board members pushed back.

title: Oregon education funding committee recommends increasing school spending by $2.5B to $5B
summary: The Quality Education Commission's 2026 report estimates schools need nearly $2.5B more to maintain current service in 2027-29 and nearly $5B more to meet new accountability and attendance targets. Personnel costs drive most K-12 spending.

quotes.speaker: QEC report, as quoted by OPB

title: Kotek's executive order to reset student instructional time fans flames in Portland
summary: Kotek's executive order bars districts from cutting instructional time and requires restoring 2024-25 levels by 2027-28, without new funding attached.

title: Calls to tap state education reserves continue as PPS proposes hundreds of layoffs
summary: Pressure to use the Education Stability Fund grew as PPS proposed layoffs; Kotek said she did not expect additional school money beyond the current budget.

title: Facing a $65 million deficit, Portland Public Schools asks the state to step in
summary: PPS leaders asked the state to use $500M of the roughly $1B Education Stability Fund to buy down PERS rates for districts statewide. Using the fund requires a governor's emergency declaration and a three-fifths legislative vote.

title: School district begs state for bailout

title: Gov. Kotek says her next Oregon budget will prioritize summer learning programs
summary: At a press event at Faubion School in Northeast Portland, Kotek said education and summer learning would be priorities in her 2027-29 budget, while warning of difficult choices. The article notes Education Stability Fund conditions and pushback from the teachers' union and district leaders.

title: Governor proposes $11.36 billion State School Fund for 2025-27
summary: Kotek proposed an $11.36B State School Fund for 2025-27, an 11% increase; the 2023-25 SSF was $10.2B. The 2024 QEM estimated a $12.7B SSF was needed.
